newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: QUALITY SEEN FOCUS IN S.AFRICAN FRUIT DEREGULATION.
newsitem.headline: QUALITY SEEN FOCUS IN S.AFRICAN FRUIT DEREGULATION.

text.p: Quality control would become even more important when the deciduous fruit industry was deregulated later this year, Unifruco public affairs manager Fred Meintjies said on Monday.

In terms of the new Agricultural Marketing Act, Unifruco's statutory dominance of the export marketing of deciduous fruit will come to an end after September, opening up the way for newcomers already testing the market.
Meintjies told Reuters that the biggest change would be that Unifruco would have to negotiate contracts with individual producers, instead of just with the Deciduous Fruit Board.
There were about 2,000 deciduous fruit producers, of which about 100 produced 60 percent of the crop.
"They have all been visited and they all have the contracts in their possession," Meintjies said.

"Many of them have signed already, some of them are still discussing certain clarifications, but we are impressed with their reaction to this and most are looking forward to becoming preferred suppliers to Unifruco."
Producers who had a poor track record on quality would not be offered contracts.

"We are looking forward to placing more emphasis on quality for our key customers and we know that the vast majority of producers are supporting this stance of ours and are gearing themselves up to be part of this new system," he said.
"There will be a few growers who will want to do their own thing and we accept that."

Just who would be Unifruco's main competitors still had to emerge. A few firms started exporting under special licences last season but Meintjies said Unifruco was confident that the bulk of its suppliers would prefer to stay with it and benefit from the expertise and infrastructure that it had built up over the years.
